title: You'd Need an Oxygen Mask at 5,072 m — This Train Makes Its Own | China Travel Expert
description:
Everyone assumes you'd need an oxygen mask at 5,000 metres. On China's highest railway, you don't — the train makes its own oxygen.

The Qinghai–Tibet Railway from Xining to Lhasa is the highest railway on Earth: its top point, Tanggula Pass, sits at 5,072 m, and Tanggula is the world's highest station. More than 960 km of the Golmud–Lhasa section runs above 4,000 m, where the air holds roughly 40% less oxygen than at sea level. So the carriages are sealed and pressurised like an aircraft, with a dual oxygen-enrichment system that switches on after Golmud station — passengers just breathe normally and watch the plateau roll by.

🧭 Expert Tip: spend a night in Xining (about 2,300 m) before you board — arriving already part-acclimatised beats going from sea level straight onto the roof of the world.
